A question naming a bounded set of real subjects reaches a terminal that ANSWERS about them -- committing the set without rendering anything is not a satisfied bounded-subject-set claim.
invariants.$comment: CHAOS-3534, added deliberately as a RED invariant (team-lead ruling, 2026-08-07). Without it this case would go GREEN on its other two invariants the moment the scope-outcome and ledger fixes land -- scope_resolution_outcome_in would see 'exact' and resolution_path_in would see 'deterministic-exact', both true -- while the product still REFUSES the question. The run terminates feature_not_enabled because the v1 surface cannot render a cohort (D1, subject_preflight's committed_cohort_v1_only). This case's `proves` claim is 'bounded project/team subject sets'; a run that commits both subjects and then declines to say anything about them does not prove that. An inaccurate coverage claim is worse than an admitted gap, because a reader who sees green stops checking. So this invariant is EXPECTED TO FAIL until the D1 render gap is closed, and its failure is the honest residual, not a defect in the case. Do not 'fix' it by relaxing expected_public_outcome to unsupported -- that would cement today's refusal as the specification. NOTE the profile's expected_public_outcome ('answered_with_gaps') was derived by reading terminal_frames.wrap_legacy_answer_as_frame, which describes the LEGACY path; on the wave_3_1 preflight-enabled stack this run terminates in preflight and never reaches that function. The value is right as a GOAL and is left as declared for that reason.

$comment_known_red_own_finding_corrected: KNOWN-RED ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE, TRACKED AS CHAOS-3534. Still deliberately NOT part of the CHAOS-3533 class. CORRECTION (2026-08-07): the mechanism previously recorded here was REFUTED BY EXECUTION, and is corrected rather than silently rewritten. This note used to say the run reached 'unresolved with no ledger at all', that D2 (subject_preflight, CHAOS-3301) presupposes a cohort can reach two exactly-resolved mentions, and that 'fixing 3533 would not move it'. All three are wrong. Driving the real QuestionInterpreter + SubjectPreflight + DevOrchestrator with this exact question and both repositories seeded shows: BOTH mentions extract, BOTH resolve exact_match, a real dev_subject_set.v1 is committed, and D2 is never consulted -- D2 exists for PARTIAL cohorts, and this cohort omits nothing. The run then terminates on D1 ('committed_cohort_v1_only'): the v1 surface cannot RENDER a cohort. So the two observed symptoms had two different causes. (a) The empty ledger WAS the CHAOS-3533 class after all -- a terminate persisted at most one row, so both exact_match entries were discarded; that half is fixed by CHAOS-3533 and now derives 'deterministic-exact', exactly as this case's profile declares. (b) scope_resolution_outcome='unresolved' is this case's OWN defect and is NOT fixed by (a): that value comes from the wire scope.resolved event, not the ledger, and contracts_v2.compat.scope_resolution_from_frame had only three branches (candidates -> ambiguous, subject_ref -> ambiguous, else -> UNRESOLVED). A committed-cohort frame carries neither of the first two, so CHAOS-3497 published 'unresolved' for a run that resolved every named subject exactly. Fixed by sourcing the published resolution from the preflight's own subject_set, gated on cohort_complete. THIS CASE IS STILL EXPECTED TO BE RED, and on purpose. Its third invariant (public_outcome_in) was added precisely so it cannot go green on the two fixes above while the product still REFUSES the question -- the D1 cohort render gap is real, is CHAOS-3297/3298 territory, and is tracked as CHAOS-3551. Do not fold this back into CHAOS-3533, do not strip any invariant, and do not relax expected_public_outcome to match today's refusal.
